The office does not run title searches, give legal advice or prepare documents. Have the deed drafted ahead of time by your closing agent or lawyer. Recording payments can be made at the counter, and the recorder's page also links an online payment portal and a land records search.

What layout rules apply to a Hocking County deed?

The recorder's page explains that House Bill 525 created the layout standards, now section 317.114 of the Revised Code, effective July 1, 2009. A deed that falls short costs $20 more. What counts as conforming:

  • Type of 10 point or larger, in black or blue ink, with no highlighting anywhere.
  • One inch of margin on both sides and the bottom of each sheet.
  • Three inches clear at the top of page one for the recorder, auditor and engineer, and an inch and a half on later pages.

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD-214 discharges, state or federal documents and anything signed before the law took effect are outside the rule. A deed you draft yourself is not.

What kinds of papers does the Hocking County Recorder file?

The county's list is long, and a seller's file may touch several items on it. Deeds can be warranty, quit claim, survivorship or sheriff's deeds. Mortgage papers include releases, assumptions, assignments, subordinations and waivers of priority. The office also files certificates of transfer, affidavits, easements, leases, land contracts, plats, condominium records, powers of attorney and trusts.

Liens deserve a second look because a title search will find them. The list names these:

  • Mechanic's liens and notices of commencement.
  • Federal tax liens and personal tax liens.
  • Workers' compensation and unemployment compensation liens.
  • Child support liens and Medicaid fraud liens.

A seller who knows of one should say so early. The list also shows that annexations, street name changes and vacated streets and alleys are recorded here, which can affect a rural lot's frontage.

What does the Hocking County Auditor handle on a transfer?

The auditor sees the deed first and collects the Ohio conveyance fee, so call 740-385-2127 for the figure on your sale price. The auditor's tools menu includes a calculator that adds a parcel transfer fee to its answer. Ask at the same time whether the county levies a real property transfer tax, since that is optional for each county.

A January 2026 message on the auditor's site says short-term rentals are now valued apart from residential property, at their market value as short-term rentals. Anyone selling a cabin near the state park should ask how the parcel is classified before quoting taxes to a buyer.

The same message says the budget commission, commissioners and township trustees trimmed inside millage so collections stayed near the 2024 level after the 2025 valuation update. Without that, the auditor estimates the county's inside millage would have drawn about $1.25 million more, a 22% increase.

How can a Hocking County owner reduce or contest a tax bill?

The treasurer's page on reducing taxes lists several routes. The owner occupancy credit, once called the 2 1/2% reduction, requires that you own the home, live in it as your main residence, and apply with the auditor between January 1 and the first Monday in June. It excludes rentals, corporate or partnership owners, units in commercial buildings, taxed manufactured homes and acreage beyond one acre.

Disagreeing with the value? The Board of Revision, made up of the treasurer, the auditor and the president of the commissioners, hears appeals filed with the auditor from January 1 through March 31. The best evidence is a recent sale price shown by closing papers, or sales of comparable homes, plus photographs of the property's condition.

A late-payment penalty can be removed on request for these reasons:

  • The owner never received a correct bill and tried to get one.
  • The payment was mailed by the due date with a proper postmark but never processed.
  • Serious injury, death or a hospital stay within 60 days before the due date, with payment inside 60 days after it.
  • An error by the auditor or treasurer.
  • Reasonable cause without willful neglect, for owners timely in each of the last three years.

How do taxes and the land bank touch a Hocking County sale?

The Hocking County Treasurer is in Suite 201 of the courthouse, phone 740-385-3517. The treasurer's page says new legislation pushed the 2026 second-half collection date for real estate and mobile homes to August 7, 2026. That date has passed, so anyone who sold around it should ask the treasurer to confirm that both halves posted.

The auditor describes five state tax bills signed December 19, 2025. House Bill 186 raises the owner occupancy credit from 2.5% toward 15.38% by tax year 2029 and phases out the 10% non-business credit, and House Bill 335 slows growth in inside millage to the rate of inflation. Most of that shows up on bills from 2027 on.

The county also runs a land bank. Its page says the bank acquires vacant, abandoned and tax-foreclosed properties, waives delinquent taxes on property it takes, and deed-restricts residential parcels to prevent nightly rentals. Owners of worthless or low-value parcels can offer them to the bank instead of leaving them to a tax foreclosure.

The land bank page also says the bank is governed by a five-member board that includes the county treasurer, two commissioners, the mayor of the largest municipality and one member with real estate experience. Residential houses it sells go to buyers who show a need for single-family housing and agree to owner-occupy.

Which Hocking County housing figures help set a price?

The Census Bureau puts Hocking County at 27,512 people in July 2025 and 13,024 housing units. Its 2020 to 2024 survey shows owners in 78.8% of occupied homes, a typical home value of $186,400, typical rent of $808 and household income of about $62,960. The average commute runs 30.3 minutes, the longest among the three counties in the Census table used for this region.

About 70.6% of residents lived in rural areas in 2020, and a piece of the Wayne National Forest and Hocking Hills State Park both fall inside the county line. The Hocking River drains about half the county, and Salt Creek drains much of the southwest.

Lodging and restaurant sales of roughly $89 million in 2022 were the highest of the three counties, which points to a visitor economy. A seller near the park should not assume every buyer wants a year-round home.

A flat $39 covers the first two pages, and each extra page adds $8, including a $5 restoration fee. A deed that breaks the layout rules adds $20.

When does the Hocking County Recorder stop taking documents?

At 3:30 p.m. on weekdays. The office stays open to visitors until 4:00, and the research room closes at 3:45.

Can I order a copy of a recorded deed by email?

Yes. Emailed copies cost $2 per page, and requests should arrive by 3:30 p.m. A copy printed at the office costs $1 per page.

Who collects the Ohio conveyance fee in Hocking County?

The county auditor. Section 319.54(G)(3) sets the larger of $1 or ten cents per $100 of value, and the auditor's calculator shows the figure with a parcel transfer fee.

Will the recorder write my deed or check my title?

No. The office says it cannot perform title searches, give legal advice or prepare documents, so leave those steps to a closing agent or attorney.

What will I find at the Holmes County Recorder's office on Clinton Street?

The Recorder keeps Holmes County's land records at 75 E. Clinton Street, Suite 101, Millersburg, OH 44654. Phone (330) 674-5916, fax (330) 674-0782. A card, a check or cash all work at the counter, deeds included, according to the county's overview page.

Holmes County was cut from Coshocton, Tuscarawas and Wayne counties in 1824, and Millersburg became its seat. The overview page lists the records held in Suite 101:

  • deeds, mortgages and leases
  • liens for mechanics, workers' compensation, unemployment and federal taxes
  • partnerships, UCC financing statements and soldier's discharges
  • plats

Most sellers touch only two of these, the deed they sign and any mortgage release the lender files after payoff.

Why does a Holmes County deed visit so many offices first?

Because Holmes County's conveyance standards, effective March 1, 2019, demand a description review before the Auditor or Recorder sees the paper. Tax Map Office approval is mandatory for every legal description, plat, land contract, mineral deed and access easement.

The county is rural to its core: the Census Bureau reported under 0.1% of residents living in urban areas in 2020, and Wikipedia says about 48% of residents were Amish that year, the densest Amish population anywhere. Farm tracts that pass between families often carry old metes and bounds wording, and that is what the Tax Map staff read line by line. In the 2020 to 2024 data the average household here holds 3.26 people, far above the 2.29 to 2.50 range in Huron, Jackson and Jefferson counties.

Budget one workday for each submission. The standards promise 24 hours between drop-off and pick-up, with longer waits for complex files. A draft can be reviewed early, which keeps the signed deed from bouncing.

In what order do the Holmes County offices handle a deed?

The conveyance-by-mail sheet sets out four stops. Each has its own forms and fees, and mailed paper needs a stamped, pre-addressed envelope for every stop.

StepOfficeLocationRole
1Tax Map Office75 E. Clinton St., Suite 102, (330) 674-6631Reviews the description, 24-hour period
2Planning Commission2 Court St., Suite 2, (330) 674-8625Stamps papers that need its approval
3County Auditor75 E. Clinton St., Suite 107Collects conveyance and transfer fees
4County Recorder75 E. Clinton St., Suite 101Records the deed

Source: Holmes County conveyance-by-mail instructions. The Auditor looks for the Tax Map and Planning Commission stamps before touching a file, so a skipped stop freezes everything behind it.

What does the Holmes County Auditor take from a seller?

The fee schedule in the county standards prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of sale price as the conveyance fee and $0.50 for each parcel on the document as the transfer fee. That schedule is dated January 1, 1989, so confirm both numbers with the Auditor before you set a closing date. State law assigns the bill to the grantor, meaning the seller (R.C. 319.202(D)).

  • Write the check to the Holmes County Auditor and send recording fees separately.
  • The office returns no change on an overpaid check and will not accept a signed blank check.
  • A check stopped on a transfer is referred to the county Prosecutor.
  • Attach form DTE 100, or DTE 100EX when the transfer qualifies for an exemption. Homestead property adds DTE 101 and current agricultural use land adds DTE 102.

Moving a mobile home title takes one more stamp. The Auditor will not process that transfer until the Treasurer's stamp shows the home's taxes are paid.

What will the Holmes County Recorder bill for a deed?

The latest fee notice on the Recorder's announcements page is dated 2019. It set most documents at $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 per page after that, citing R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. Senate Bill 94 later amended the statute, effective October 24, 2024, so a county may now tack on a preservation surcharge of as much as five dollars. Phone the office for the total on your page count.

Formatting can raise the bill. R.C. 317.114 sets the layout, and a nonconforming paper is still recorded for an extra $10.00 service charge plus a $10.00 housing trust fund charge. The layout calls for:

  • 10-point type or larger in black or blue ink, with no highlighting
  • pages between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches
  • one inch of margin at each side and the foot of every page
  • three blank inches at the head of page one, and an inch and a half on later pages

The rule skips court and taxing-authority papers, plats, DD-214s and state or federal documents.

How do I search Holmes County records or e-record a deed?

Two search tools sit on the Recorder's page. AVA needs no login and fits a one-time lookup. Laredo Anywhere is for people who search often, and the county posts a setup guide in its document library. Both show images of deeds, easements, rights-of-way and leases. Other record types can be viewed from 1980 forward, and plats live on the Tax Map Department website.

The office accepts documents electronically, including deeds. It names four vendors: ePN, Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services and CSC, which serve title companies, law firms and banks that record regularly. State law (R.C. 317.13) gave every recorder until June 30, 2026 to offer electronic filing of conveyance papers, and that deadline is behind us.

Can I get a warning if someone files a paper against my Holmes County property?

The Recorder's overview page invites owners to sign up for Property Fraud Alert and points to a flyer in the Recorder section of the county document library. An alert matters most to an owner who lives away from the house or who has just inherited it, because a forged deed or an unexpected lien only shows up in the public record after it is filed.

Once a sale closes, the same office record becomes the buyer's proof of ownership. Check that the deed shows the correct parcel, the Tax Map Office stamp and the Auditor's endorsement before anything is handed over.

What do Holmes County's housing numbers look like?

QuickFacts estimates 44,970 residents for July 2025, which is 1.7% above the April 2020 base. There are 14,592 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 it puts the owner-occupied rate at 79.0%, the middle owner-occupied home at $267,700 and median household income at $76,140.

Two other figures explain why paper filing persists. Just 63.5% of households report a broadband subscription, the thinnest coverage in that four-county table, and 49.0% of people five and older speak something other than English at home. Calling or visiting Suites 101, 102 and 107 often beats an online form.

Visitors help the local economy. Wikipedia says Holmes drew the second most tourists of any Ohio county in 2017, with the Amish and Mennonite Heritage Center in Berlin among the stops.

More questions about Holmes County, OH Recorder of Deeds

Can I pay the Holmes County Recorder by credit card?

Yes. The overview page states that the office accepts cash, check and credit card, and says the same applies to deeds and other conveyance documents.

Is Tax Map approval needed before a Holmes County deed is recorded?

Yes, whenever the paper carries a legal description. The standards route all descriptions, land contracts, mineral deeds and easements to the Tax Map Office first, with a 24-hour review.

Who owes the conveyance fee on a Holmes County sale?

The seller owes it. R.C. 319.202(D) charges the grantor, and the Auditor's schedule prints $4.00 per thousand dollars of price plus $0.50 per parcel, dated January 1, 1989. Verify the figures with the Auditor.

Can a Holmes County deed go through the mail?

Yes. Follow the four-stop sheet in order, and enclose forms, fees and a pre-addressed, correctly stamped envelope for each office.

Who can obtain a recorded military discharge in Holmes County?

Only authorized parties, such as the veteran, a county veterans service officer or the heir of a deceased veteran. A discharge stays out of the public record for 75 years, and anyone else sees just name, rank, birth date, discharge date and type.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Huron County, OH Recorder of Deeds sale
  • Turn the Huron County, OH Recorder of Deeds offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Huron County? Get a Cash Offer

What we could not confirm

  • Delinquent/foreclosure not found

Huron County by the numbers

Where do I take a deed in Norwalk, and until what time?

Take it to the Huron County Recorder at 12 E. Main Street, Suite 100, Norwalk, OH 44857. The office keeps weekday hours of 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Its phone is 419-668-1916, its fax is 419-663-4052, and document requests go to Recorder@huroncounty-oh.gov.

The real cutoff is 4:20 PM. Anything submitted later is recorded the next business day, according to the office. Ohio recorders file instruments in the order they arrive and note the exact time (R.C. 317.13), so two deeds for the same house are ranked by that clock.

The same statute told every recorder to post electronic indexes and images of everything recorded since January 1, 1980 by June 30, 2026. A county may require a username and password but cannot charge for one. In Huron County, copies still come from the office.

Which charges apply when a deed is recorded in Huron County?

The Recorder posts a table effective January 1, 2025. Two pages cost $39.00, up from $34.00, because Senate Bill 94 created a $5.00 document preservation surcharge and Huron County started collecting it on the first day of that year.

PagesRecording fee
1 to 2$39.00
3$47.00
5$63.00
7$79.00
10$103.00

Source: Huron County Recorder fee table, trimmed for space. Past page two the price climbs $8.00 a page. Each marginal reference adds $4.00, and the standardization guidelines still apply. A mortgage release that points back to a recorded mortgage is the common reason for a marginal reference.

Can I record a Huron County deed online?

Yes, for nearly everything. Plats and vacation documents are the exceptions and must be mailed or brought to Norwalk. Six submitting vendors are listed:

  • Corporation Service Company (CSC)
  • eRecording Partners Network (EPN)
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile
  • Hopdox
  • File And Go

Each vendor sets its own pricing and onboarding, so contact one directly. The office also runs AlertMe, which sends a notice when a paper carrying a name you register is recorded or corrected. An owner who fears a forged filing against the family home can watch for it that way. The Public Access site searches recorded documents, and the Recorder asks that copy requests come by email or phone.

What must a deed show before the Huron County Auditor will transfer it?

Chapter 14 of the county's conveyance standards, written jointly by the Auditor and the Engineer, lists what the deed has to carry. The Tax Map Department takes files first come, first served, and splits, combinations, annexations and subdivisions can run several days.

  • the grantor's original signature, or a certified copy of a court order
  • the volume and page of the last recorded deed in the chain of title
  • the grantee's full tax mailing address
  • the full names of grantor and grantee
  • the Auditor's parcel number and the site address
  • a completed DTE 100, or the exemption form when the transfer is exempt

The standards suggest a pre-transfer check at the Tax Map Department before anyone signs. The Auditor is at 12 E. Main Street, Suite 300, phone (419) 668-4304, on weekday hours that match the Recorder's.

What does the DTE 100 ask a Huron County seller to disclose?

The form is the statement of value that travels with the deed. It breaks the price into a new mortgage, any balance assumed and cash, then subtracts whatever was paid for items other than real property. The conveyance fee is figured on the remainder.

Two questions affect the buyer's tax bill. One asks whether the seller said the home receives the senior, disabled or surviving spouse homestead exemption, which brings in form DTE 101. The other asks about current agricultural use valuation and form DTE 102. A final item is the owner-occupancy application for the 2.5% reduction on qualified levies, and the form warns that skipping it blocks the reduction until a new proper and timely application is filed.

The Auditor's receipt on the form covers the fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3) and, where one exists, the Chapter 322 fee. Ask the Auditor what rate is in force.

Which Huron County Auditor forms matter to someone selling a home?

Besides the conveyance forms, the Auditor's Forms page carries the tax applications a seller or buyer may need around closing. Several concern relief that either helps the seller or has to be reapplied for by the buyer:

  • DTE 105A and 105B, the homestead exemption applications for senior citizens, disabled persons and surviving spouses
  • DTE 105I, the homestead application for disabled veterans and surviving spouses
  • DTE 105C, the 2.5% reduction on an owner-occupied home
  • DTE 26, the valuation deduction for damaged or destroyed real property
  • DTE 23A, the remission of late-payment penalties
  • DTE 1, the complaint against the valuation of real property

The seller's own homestead status is disclosed on the DTE 100, and the buyer should file the owner-occupancy application when the house will be a principal residence. The Auditor's home page keeps a link to current homestead information.

Who can sign a deed for the Huron County Recorder, and why record it?

The grantor signs, and under R.C. 5301.01 the signature is acknowledged before a judge or court clerk, a county auditor, a county engineer, a notary or a mayor. Most sellers use the notary at a title company or bank.

Recording follows. R.C. 5301.25 treats an unrecorded deed as fraudulent against a later buyer who paid without knowing of it, which is why closing agents file the same day.

The Recorder may decline a paper that is not required or authorized to be recorded, or that looks materially false or fraudulent. Someone refused can ask the Huron County Court of Common Pleas for an order. The Recorder has no duty to inspect a deed for mistakes, so the preparer must check the legal description, each name and the notary block. A deed returned for a defect loses its place in line.

What is Huron County like for a homeowner?

Huron County lies in the Firelands, the western section of Connecticut's old Western Reserve, which is why many townships carry Connecticut names. It was created in 1809, organized in 1815, and Norwalk serves as seat. The Norwalk micropolitan area belongs to the Cleveland-Akron-Canton combined area.

QuickFacts estimates 58,250 residents for July 2025, a 0.5% slip since the 2020 base. Housing units total 25,763, and 74.0% of homes are owner-occupied. The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $166,000, median gross rent is $848 and median household income is $67,878. Hispanic or Latino residents make up 7.9% of the population, the highest share among Holmes, Jackson and Jefferson counties.

The 23,490 households average 2.45 people, and 88.4% have a broadband subscription, so online searching and e-filing reach most homes. Wikipedia places the Norwalk-Huron County Airport three nautical miles east of downtown Norwalk, and the county touches seven other Ohio counties, Erie to the north and Richland to the south among them.

More questions about Huron County, OH Recorder of Deeds

How much does the Huron County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?

$47.00, per the table effective January 1, 2025. Pages one and two total $39.00, the third adds $8.00, and a $4.00 charge applies to each marginal reference.

When does a Huron County deed miss same-day recording?

After 4:20 PM. The office says later submissions are recorded the next business day, though it stays open until 4:30 PM on weekdays.

Can I view recorded Huron County documents from home?

The Public Access site searches the records, but the Recorder tells users to visit or contact the office for copies. Email Recorder@huroncounty-oh.gov or call 419-668-1916.

Do plats go through e-recording in Huron County?

No. Plats and vacation documents are the two types left out of electronic recording and must be mailed or delivered to the Norwalk office.

Who approves a legal description in Huron County?

The County Auditor and the County Engineer, under R.C. 315.251 and 319.203. They may reject a nonconforming description and are expected to work out technical problems informally with the presenter.

Where in the Jackson County Courthouse do I file a deed?

Go upstairs to the third floor. The Recorder sits inside the courthouse at 226 East Main Street, Jackson, OH 45640, phone (740) 286-1919, fax (740) 286-8835. The county page says the office runs 8:30 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays and shuts for lunch between 11:30 am and 12:30 pm, so plan to arrive outside that gap.

Payment may be cash, a check or a debit or credit card, and the card route adds a $2.00 service fee. The county's official records begin in 1997. Anything older must be viewed and printed at the office, while later records are searchable online after you set up an account.

What are the Jackson County Recorder's listed prices?

The county's fee page puts most recordable papers, from deeds and mortgages to leases and affidavits, at $39.00 for two pages and $8.00 for every further page, counting each printed side separately. It explains that Ohio sets these amounts, with one half paying for the basic recording fee and the other half going to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund.

ItemFee
Recording a deed, mortgage or lease (two pages included)$39.00
Each page past two$8.00

Source: Jackson County Recorder fee page. A veteran's service discharge and one certified copy carry no fee, and a zoning resolution costs $50.00.

What does the Jackson County Auditor add ahead of recording?

Two charges are printed on the Auditor's real estate transfers page: a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand and a transfer fee of fifty cents per parcel. A history note records that on March 24, 1993 the conveyance fee jumped from $1.00 per thousand of the purchase price.

The Auditor works in the same building, 226 East Main Street, Suite 5, phone (740) 286-4231, opening at 8:00 am and closing at 4:00 pm. Under the Auditor's Tools menu you will find a Conveyance Calculator and a Sales Reports page. The seller carries the cost, since R.C. 319.202(D) charges the grantor. Forms on the site include:

  • DTE 100, the value statement that doubles as the fee receipt
  • DTE 100EX, the reason an exemption applies
  • DTE 100M and 100MEX, the manufactured and mobile home versions

The order is Auditor, then Recorder. The Recorder's site is blunt about changes of names: adding or removing someone requires a new deed that clears the Auditor and is then recorded.

What goes wrong if a Jackson County deed is never recorded?

A second buyer can end up owning the house. R.C. 5301.25 requires a deed to be recorded in the county of the land, and until that happens it is treated as fraudulent against a later purchaser who bought in good faith.

The Recorder's own site answers three things sellers ask:

  • Most records are public. Military service records go only to the veteran, with proof of ID.
  • A will is recorded through Probate Court, which the site prices at $46.00.
  • Deeds and similar papers are best drafted by an attorney or other professional, in the office's view.

A name error means a fresh deed, which repeats the Auditor and Recorder steps.

How do I order copies or search Jackson County records?

Viewing most records online starts with an account, as the county's Recorder page directs. A deed from the 1980s predates the 1997 start of the official records and has to be pulled at the courthouse itself.

Ordering an image works by email: send the document's book and page to recordersoffice@jacksoncounty.us. The charge is $2.00 a page, paid in cash or by check. Someone planning to list a house can also open the Sales Reports page on the Auditor's site, which sits alongside the Conveyance Calculator and a Tax Estimator.

Which other papers does the Jackson County Recorder file, and what do they cost?

The fee page covers more than deeds. These items surface when a title search finds old liens or a former owner left paperwork behind:

  • federal tax liens and other federal liens: $5.00
  • releases or partial releases of those liens: $3.00
  • a living will or durable power of attorney for health care: $40.00
  • zoning amendments: $20.00
  • no fee for personal property tax, workers' compensation, recognizance and unemployment compensation liens, or for certificates of premium due

The county ties these charges to R.C. 317.32 and 317.36. If an old lien shows up on your parcel, ask the Recorder which release clears it and what that costs, because a release is recorded on its own, apart from the deed.

Can a new owner contest a Jackson County valuation after buying?

Yes, by a complaint to the county Board of Revision. As the Auditor's complaint page describes it, the board is the Auditor, the Treasurer and the President of the County Commissioners, or their designees, and it changes values rather than tax dollars. A complaint is filed on form DTE 1 with the Auditor, who acts as the board's secretary, and the Auditor's public notice gives March 31 as the filing deadline.

The page adds several cautions. The form must show the owner's opinion of value on line 8 and be notarized. Ohio allows one filing per three-year period in general, and a withdrawn complaint still counts. Proof falls on the owner, and the outcome can be a higher value, a lower one or no change. The board will not weigh a percentage jump in the tax bill or a neighbor's lower valuation.

For payment questions, the Auditor's site sends people to the County Treasurer at 740-286-2402. Real estate taxes can be paid online or by the Autoagent phone line, 1-844-674-1100.

What is Jackson County like for a homeowner?

Jackson County was founded on March 1, 1818 and carries the name of Andrew Jackson. Wikipedia calls it the Little Wales of Ohio. The Hanging Rock Iron Region shaped its past. The Jefferson Iron Furnace went up in 1854, county iron went into the USS Monitor, and coal and salt mining followed. Furnace remnants stand in Jackson Lake State Park, and Wayne National Forest takes in part of the county.

QuickFacts estimates 32,817 residents for July 2025. It lists 14,665 housing units, 73.9% owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied home is worth $150,700, and median household income is $57,106. Commutes average 29.4 minutes, longer than in Holmes, Huron or Jefferson counties, and poverty affects 15.5% of residents. The Auditor's site counts 28,916 parcels for 2024 and 422 square miles of total area. The 12,933 households average 2.50 people, 84.3% have broadband, and the Census Bureau logged 30 building permits for 2025. Vinton, Gallia, Lawrence, Scioto, Pike and Ross counties surround it.

More questions about Jackson County, OH Recorder of Deeds

How much does the Jackson County Recorder charge for a three-page deed?

$47.00 on the fee page's formula, which is $39.00 for the first two pages plus $8.00 for the third. Each marginal notation adds $4.00, so ask the office whether any apply to your paper.

Is the Jackson County Recorder open over lunch?

No. The office shuts from 11:30 am to 12:30 pm, according to the county page, and its weekday service window is 8:30 am to 4:00 pm.

What conveyance fee does Jackson County charge?

$4.00 per thousand dollars of purchase price, plus a $0.50 transfer fee for each parcel, per the Auditor's page. The $4.00 rate dates to March 24, 1993.

Does paying the Jackson County Recorder by card cost extra?

Yes, by $2.00. The Recorder's site accepts debit and credit cards with that service fee, while cash and checks carry no add-on.

Does the Jackson County Recorder record wills?

No. The Recorder's site says a will is recorded in Probate Court and gives the cost as $46.00. The Recorder files deeds, mortgages and similar land records.

Jefferson County by the numbers

What happens at the Recorder's counter in Steubenville?

This is where the permanent record is kept of each paper that moves land, secures a mortgage or adds some other charge on a Jefferson County parcel. The office is at 301 Market Street, Steubenville, OH 43952. A statewide legal aid directory shows it open weekdays, opening at 8:30 in the morning and closing at 4:30 in the afternoon. Ask for the current fee schedule before you go. The county's 2025 financial report counts five employees in the Recorder's office, so send complete packets and call ahead.

Jefferson County runs along the Ohio River and the West Virginia line, with Steubenville as seat and largest city. The county's financial report counts 14 townships inside its 410 square miles, with Columbiana County on the north and Belmont County on the south, as the report describes the area. Every parcel in the county is recorded here, whether it sits in Steubenville, in Toronto, the one other city, or out in a village or township. Property across the river in Brooke or Hancock County, West Virginia, falls under West Virginia's own recording system.

What goes into a recording fee on a Jefferson County deed?

Under R.C. 317.32 every charge pairs a recorder's base fee with an equal fee for the Ohio housing trust fund. Get the Recorder's total for your paper before writing a check. The statute's pieces are:

  • pages one and two: seventeen dollars to the recorder and seventeen to the trust fund
  • every later page, or fraction of a page, at legal size: four dollars and four dollars
  • each marginal reference entered by a separate instrument: two dollars and two dollars
  • a certified copy: one dollar and one dollar a page, with fifty cents and fifty cents more for the seal
  • an optional preservation surcharge, up to five dollars, that stays in the county's general fund

The surcharge entered the statute through Senate Bill 94, effective October 24, 2024. Only the Recorder can say whether Jefferson County charges it and how much.

Which conveyance charges does a Steubenville-area seller owe?

Two layers are collected at the Auditor's counter. The Auditor's own fee, in R.C. 319.54(G)(3), is the larger of one dollar or ten cents for each hundred dollars of value, fractions counted. Beyond it, a county may adopt a transfer tax under R.C. 322.02, limited to thirty cents on each hundred dollars.

In its 2025 annual financial report, Jefferson County refers to a four mill permissive conveyance fee and says one of those mills is dedicated to the GIS Fund by the commissioners. The Auditor is at 301 Market Street, P.O. Box 159, Steubenville, with phone (740) 283-8511 and fax (740) 283-8520. Confirm the rate with that office, since a permissive levy is set by commissioner resolution.

The seller pays, per R.C. 319.202(D). An exempt transfer travels with a statement of the exemption's basis instead of the fee.

Which family transfers in Jefferson County skip the conveyance fee?

About two dozen exemptions appear in R.C. 319.54(G)(3). These are the ones a family handling a house in the county is likely to meet:

  • a gift between husband and wife, or to a child from a parent, or to the spouse of either
  • a deed among the heirs or devisees of the same decedent, with no money paid
  • a deed into a trust that its maker can revoke at will
  • a deed that corrects or confirms one already of record
  • an interest worth one hundred dollars or less
  • a transfer by court order, except one that results from a sale under that order

A sale to an outside buyer is a different matter. Even a fast as-is sale for cash is a fee-paying transfer, and the seller covers the fee at closing.

Who employs the people buying homes in Jefferson County?

The county's 2025 annual financial report ranks ten large employers, and the table shows the top five. The report puts total county employment at 26,800.

EmployerBusinessEmployees
Trinity Health SystemAcute care hospital1,917
Wal-Mart Distribution CenterRetail food sales distribution1,014
Titanium Metals CorporationTitanium mill production780
Jefferson County GovernmentLocal government621
Franciscan UniversityHigher education577

Source: Jefferson County Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for 2025. The same report puts 2025 unemployment at 4.90% and population at 63,597, which ranks 39th among Ohio's 88 counties. Wikipedia traces the county's industrial turn to 1856, when a rolling mill was built and a coal shaft sunk.

How do Jefferson County housing figures compare?

QuickFacts lists 30,964 housing units for July 2025, with 70.5% occupied by their owners. Its 2020 to 2024 figures put a typical owner-occupied home at $127,800, monthly gross rent at $835 and household income at $59,055. Residents 65 and older make up 23.9% of the county, a bigger share than in Holmes, Huron or Jackson, and 17.7% of people are in poverty.

Census data show 27,143 households averaging 2.29 people, 3,559 veterans and 86.6% broadband adoption. The head count slid 2.5% from the 2020 base to July 2025, the steepest drop of the four counties. The Weirton-Steubenville metropolitan area, which adds Brooke and Hancock counties in West Virginia, is the labor market most residents work in.

In what order do the Auditor and Recorder act on a Jefferson County deed?

The Auditor is first in line. Any county transfer tax is owed by the grantor, payable to the auditor at delivery of the deed and ahead of presentation to the recorder (R.C. 322.02). The Auditor marks the fee amount on the deed, which then moves on to the Recorder.

Ohio gave county recorders, auditors and engineers until June 30, 2026 to provide electronic recording of conveyance papers (R.C. 317.13), and that deadline has gone by. A Steubenville title company can file a closing package electronically instead of carrying it across the floor. A seller handling a deed alone should bring the signed, notarized original if the office wants paper.

How did Steubenville and Jefferson County begin?

The United States built Fort Steuben in 1786 to protect surveyors mapping land west of the Ohio River. Settlers built homes around it, calling the place La Belle at first, and the town was later renamed Steubenville for the fort. La Belle was picked as county seat when the county was created. Through the first half of the 19th century Steubenville worked mainly as a port, while the rest of the county held small villages and farms. The county was organized on July 29, 1797, six years ahead of Ohio statehood, and reached its current boundaries in 1833 once Carroll County was formed.

Route 7 carries traffic north and south through the county, and U.S. Route 22 leads east toward Pittsburgh International Airport. About 408 square miles of land are bounded by Columbiana, Belmont, Carroll and Harrison counties and by West Virginia.

More questions about Jefferson County, OH Recorder of Deeds

Which office records the deed on a house in Steubenville?

The Jefferson County Recorder, 301 Market Street. Steubenville lies inside Jefferson County, so its deeds are filed there.

Does Jefferson County charge the optional document preservation surcharge?

Ask the Recorder. R.C. 317.32 allows a surcharge of up to five dollars, and the office can tell you what it adds to a deed.

Who pays the conveyance fee on a Jefferson County sale?

The seller does. R.C. 319.202(D) assigns the Auditor's fee, and any Chapter 322 transfer tax the county levies, to the grantor.

Is a gift from a parent to a child exempt from the conveyance fee in Jefferson County?

Yes. Subdivision (d) of R.C. 319.54(G)(3) covers it. The deed still passes through the Auditor with an exemption statement before recording.

What is the four mill fee in the Jefferson County financial report?

It is the county's permissive conveyance fee. The 2025 report says the commissioners dedicated one mill of the four mill fee to the county's GIS Fund, which keeps the parcel maps current.

Knox County by the numbers

Where does a Knox County seller record a deed?

The recorder in Mount Vernon files Knox County deeds, but the auditor sees them first. The auditor's office is at 117 East High Street, Suite 120, Mount Vernon, OH 43050. Its published weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:00, the real estate desk answers at 740-393-6745, and the exemption desk at 740-393-6748. Phone the recorder's office for its own counter hours, payment methods and mailing rules before a deed goes in the mail.

Ohio gives each county a single recorder. Whether the house sits in town, near Fredericktown or around Gambier, the paperwork follows the same route through that one Mount Vernon office.

What does the Knox County auditor charge when a deed transfers?

The auditor's home page says Knox County's conveyance fee is $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price. Section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents per transfer or entry. After the auditor, the recorder bills under section 317.32, where each charge pairs a base fee with a housing trust fund fee.

What a Knox County deed can cost, from the auditor's home page and Ohio Revised Code sections 317.32, 317.114 and 319.54
ChargePrinted amount
Conveyance fee (auditor)$3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price
Transfer or entry (auditor)$0.50 each
Recording a two page deed$17 base fee, matched by a $17 housing trust fund fee
Every page past two$4 base fee, matched by a $4 housing trust fund fee
Preservation surchargeUp to $5, a county option
Marginal reference$2 plus $2 for each reference
Deed that ignores the layout rules$10 plus $10 on top of the usual charge

Ask the recorder whether the surcharge applies and what your page count totals.

Who files the statement of value, and who pays?

The buyer files it, and the seller pays, under section 319.202. The figure reported is the full price, mortgage included, and a false number is a violation. A county transfer tax, if one is levied, is collected the same way before the deed moves on to the recorder.

Knox County's auditor posts these forms for a sale:

  • DTE 100 records the statement of value and doubles as the receipt.
  • DTE 100(EX) names the reason a deed owes nothing.
  • DTE 101 discloses a conveyance of homestead property.
  • DTE 102 covers land enrolled in the current agricultural use valuation, common on farm acreage here.

The statute asks the buyer to affirm that the seller was questioned about any homestead reduction and any farm valuation. Tell the closing agent about either one early.

Which Knox County deeds owe no conveyance fee?

The exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3) is long. The entries a homeowner is likeliest to use:

  • Gifts between spouses, or from a parent to a child.
  • Transfers among a decedent's heirs when no money changes hands.
  • Deeds into a trust the maker can revoke, and deeds back out of it.
  • Corrective deeds that repair an earlier recorded one.
  • Interests worth $100 or less.

Government, charity and court-ordered transfers appear on the list too. An exempt deed still needs the exemption form, so ask the real estate desk which form fits.

How must a deed be laid out for the Knox County recorder?

Section 317.114 asks for ten point type or larger, paper between letter and legal size, dark ink, no highlighter, one inch margins on the sides and bottom, and a three inch clear band across the top of page one. The recorder will still take a deed that misses these, at the added cost shown in the table. Court filings, plats, agency papers and instruments signed before July 1, 2009 are outside the rule.

What is Knox County like beyond the courthouse?

Knox County split off from Fairfield County in 1808 and carries the name of Henry Knox. It spans 525.50 square miles of land at about 119 people per square mile, with rolling hills in the glaciated Allegheny Plateau. Wikipedia puts farmland near 58 percent of the county and forest near 28 percent, and Mount Vernon is the single city.

Census QuickFacts counts 64,002 people in mid 2025, a gain of 2.0 percent since April 2020, in 26,668 housing units. Three out of four homes are owner occupied (75.5 percent). Home values: $239,400 median for 2020 to 2024. Rent: $950 median gross. Households: 23,491, at a median income of $73,878. Eighty nine percent of households have broadband (89.3 percent), 91.0 percent of adults finished high school and 24.7 percent hold a bachelor's degree. About 89.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 270 building permits were issued in 2025.

The local payroll includes Siemens Energy and Ariel Corporation in Mount Vernon, Kenyon College in Gambier, Mount Vernon Nazarene University and Kokosing Construction near Fredericktown, and agriculture is large, with corn the main crop.

What can a Knox County owner check on the auditor's site before listing?

The auditor runs a real estate search portal that was upgraded for use on phones and tablets, plus a tax estimator, a GIS and tax map page and a downloadable property data correction form. If a deed splits acreage, the forms page carries a split form and a form for the proposed division of valuation on split acreage, which matters for owners selling off a lot from a larger farm parcel.

  • Run the parcel search and compare the owner name and acreage with your deed.
  • Try the tax estimator for a rough tax figure to show a buyer.
  • Download the property data correction form if a record shows the wrong square footage or building count.
  • Read the sheriff sales page if the parcel has a case in court.

The auditor's home page adds that the office does not give out phone numbers for property owners, so buyers and agents should contact you through the listing.

When are Knox County real estate taxes due, and where do disputes go?

For 2026 the auditor's page lists February 13 and August 26, and both dates are past. Ask the Knox County Treasurer for the next pair. The auditor links to the treasurer's payment site from its home page.

Value complaints go to the Knox County Board of Revision. The auditor's notice says the board organizes on January 4, 2027 and takes formal complaints from January 1 through March 31, 2027, and that the 2026 returns can be inspected at the auditor's office. The auditor's menu also links pages for the owner occupancy reduction, homestead exemption, CAUV soil rates, agricultural districts and sheriff sales.

When a tax bill is still open at closing, the title company typically gets a payoff from the treasurer and settles it from the proceeds. Request that figure as soon as a contract exists.

More questions about Knox County, OH Recorder of Deeds

Who records a deed in Knox County, Ohio?

The Knox County Recorder in Mount Vernon. The deed visits the auditor at 117 East High Street, Suite 120 beforehand. Call the recorder for current hours and mailing instructions.

What is the Knox County conveyance fee?

The auditor's home page states $3.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, and section 319.54(G)(2) adds fifty cents per transfer or entry. Under section 319.202 the seller bears it.

What if my deed ignores the margin and ink rules?

The recorder takes it anyway and collects an extra $10 base fee and $10 housing trust fund fee. Court papers, plats, agency documents and instruments from before July 1, 2009 are excluded.

Can I give a Knox County house to my child without the conveyance fee?

A gift from a parent to a child is on the exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3). File the DTE 100(EX) with the auditor. The recorder's own charges still apply.

Which forms apply to farm ground or a homestead parcel in Knox County?

The auditor lists DTE 101 for homestead property and DTE 102 for current agricultural use valuation property. Ask the auditor about any recoupment charge on farm land before closing.

How does a deed get recorded in Lake County, Ohio?

It takes two counters in Painesville. The Transfer Office (the Auditor's first floor) comes first, where you complete an Exempt Form or a Conveyance Fee Form and get the deed stamped. The Recorder, on the lower level of the Administration Building, comes second and processes the deed on the spot.

The recorder's contact page gives the street address as 105 Main Street, Lower Level, with P.O. Box 490, Painesville, OH 44077, phone (440) 350-2510 and email recorder@lakecountyohio.gov. Counter service runs weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m., closed on holidays, and the fee page asks that the day's last recordings be in before 3:45.

A mailed filing has its own checklist. Each auditor and engineer stamp has to be on the deed already, and the envelope needs a cover letter, one check for the Recorder, one for the Auditor and a stamped return envelope. If the Auditor's stamp is missing, the deed comes back rejected.

What does the Lake County Recorder charge, and what goes to the Auditor?

The Recorder bills $34.00 for a two page deed and $5.00 for preservation, and each page past the second adds $8.00. The Auditor collects its own transfer charges, which is why the office wants two checks.

Lake County deed charges listed on the Recorder's guidelines and record-a-deed pages and on the Auditor's transfer page
ItemPrinted amountPayee

Nonconforming document$20.00 penaltyRecorder

Transfer fee$0.50 for each parcelAuditor

Per the Auditor's FAQ, the $4.00 breaks into a $1.00 state share and a $3.00 county share, the county piece set by a commissioners' resolution dated March 26, 1990 under section 322.02.

What paperwork does the Lake County Auditor want with a transfer?

The Auditor's real estate FAQ answers the common questions. Either side of the deal, or a representative, may hand in the deed, and mail is accepted. Everything must be complete, signed and notarized. The Transfer Office takes transfers between 8 and 4.

  • A DTE 100 or DTE 100EX goes with every transfer.
  • Parcels in the homestead or CAUV farm programs need a notarized DTE 101 or DTE 102 first.
  • A sale of anything short of a whole platted sublot, such as a piece of a sublot or a metes and bounds tract, must clear the Tax Map Department. Exempt transfers skip that stop.
  • Taking someone off a deed means drafting a new deed, and the FAQ points owners toward a title company or attorney.

The county posts owner names exactly as the recorded deed spells them, so a typo on the deed travels into the tax records.

Which Lake County transfers are exempt from the conveyance fee?

Section 319.54(G)(3) holds the exemption list, and the reason is written on the form that section 319.202 requires. Examples that fit house sales:

  • A deed given only as security for a debt, or releasing that security.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • Survivorship transfers under sections 5302.17 or 5302.18.
  • A deed to a trustee when the maker kept an unlimited power to revoke.
  • A transfer to a non-dealer who is only a stop on the way to a prompt resale.

One shortcut shows on the Recorder's page: a Transfer on Death Beneficiary Designation Affidavit skips the Auditor and goes straight to the Recorder, with the recording fee and a return envelope.

Can a deed be e-recorded in Lake County?

Yes. The Record A Deed page names four e-recording partners: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hop Docs. You deal with one of those firms, because the Recorder's office does not operate the portal itself.

For research, the Recorder's e-recording page points to the AVA search engine for basic results and to Laredo Select for deeper searching, which needs a registered account. Filings cannot carry watermarks. The office's services menu also lists a property fraud alert and a video chat on that topic.

How should a Lake County deed be prepared?

The Recorder's guidelines restate section 317.114 and warn that a deed outside them is still accepted but costs the $20.00 penalty. Before signing, confirm:

  • Type at 10 point or bigger, on paper cut between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14.
  • Black or blue ink, with nothing highlighted.
  • One inch margins at the sides and foot, three inches clear at the top of page one for stamps, and an inch and a half on the pages after.
  • A title, a date, typed names and titles under every signature, and a notary block that shows the commission expiration.
  • The preparer's name and a full legal description.

When one document refers to an earlier one, cite its number, or its book and page, along with the recording date. Each such reference adds $4.00.

What kind of county is Lake County for a home sale?

Lake County lies on the southern shore of Lake Erie inside the Cleveland metropolitan area. Painesville is the seat and Mentor the largest city. Formed March 6, 1840, it has 227 square miles of land inside a 979 square mile total, and its lakeshore runs 31 miles. Former glacial beaches survive as ridge roads such as South Ridge, and Lake Shore Boulevard follows another old beach through Mentor Township.

Census QuickFacts: 232,217 residents in mid 2025 (roughly 1,014 per square mile) and 107,571 housing units. Ownership rate, 75.8 percent. Median value of owned homes, $214,100. Median gross rent, $1,113. Median household income, $80,925. Interstates and routes matter to buyers here: I-90 and State Route 2 run through, State Route 44 links them, and Laketran buses reach downtown Cleveland.

School district names carry weight in listings. Mentor Public, Painesville City Local, Willoughby-Eastlake City, Wickliffe City, Kirtland Local, Madison Local, Perry Local, Riverside Local and Fairport Harbor Exempted Village each cover part of the county.

What tax questions come up at a Lake County closing?

The Treasurer lists the 2026 tax payable in 2027 as due February 24 and July 21, 2027 for real estate, and bills mail out in mid-January and mid-June, per the Auditor's FAQ. A buyer's lender or the title company will ask for the status of those halves, so request the Treasurer's payoff before the closing date. The Treasurer's billing line is (440) 350-2516, and the Auditor's real estate staff answer address and credit questions at (440) 350-2532.

If a record shows a wrong owner address, the Auditor corrects owner addresses while the Treasurer handles the tax mailing address, so changes may need two calls.

More questions about Lake County, OH Recorder of Deeds

Where is the Lake County Recorder's office?

Lower Level, 105 Main Street, Painesville, OH 44077, with mail going to P.O. Box 490. The listed number is (440) 350-2510 and counter hours run weekdays from 8 to 4, closed on holidays.

What is the Lake County conveyance fee?

$4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price plus $0.50 per parcel, according to the Auditor's Real Estate FAQ. It is paid to the Auditor before the Recorder sees the deed.

Do I need two checks to record a deed in Lake County?

Yes. The guidelines want a check for each office, one made out to the Lake County Recorder and one to the Lake County Auditor. Mailed filings also need a stamped self-addressed envelope, or the originals come back collect on delivery.

When does a Lake County sale need Tax Map approval?

When money changes hands and the parcel is anything other than a full sublot in a platted subdivision. Part of a sublot and metes and bounds tracts both qualify. Exempt transfers do not need it.

Can I mail a deed to the Lake County Auditor?

Yes, mail transfers are accepted. Address them to the Auditor's Real Estate Transfer Office, 105 Main Street, PO Box 490, Painesville, OH 44077. The deed is passed to the Recorder after transfer.

Think of the office as the county's permanent land file. Its common documents page names warranty and quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds, sheriff's deeds, certificates of transfer, affidavits of transfer, life estate terminations and transfer on death designation and confirmation affidavits. It also names mortgage releases and assignments, land contracts, plats, powers of attorney, zoning maps and a long run of liens, from mechanic's liens to federal tax liens and child support liens.

A fee notice on the recorder's site says that on January 1, 2025 most recording fees went up by $5.00, the preservation surcharge that Senate Bill 94 allowed. A one or two page document now runs $39.00 and every added page costs $8.00, so the printed chart climbs by $8 a page to $103.00 at ten pages. Half of what the office collects is sent to the state for the Ohio Housing Trust Fund, consistent with section 317.32.

How do you avoid the extra $20 charge at the Lawrence County recorder?

Prepare the deed to the layout in section 317.114, which covers documents prepared after June 30, 2009. Per the office's guideline page, a deed that misses it costs $20.00 more. Its checklist:

  • Computer type of at least 10 point.
  • Sheets between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD214 discharges, state or federal documents and older instruments fall outside the rule. A margin guidelines PDF on the site helps whoever drafts the deed.

What happens at the Lawrence County auditor before a deed reaches the recorder?

The auditor is at 111 S Fourth Street, phone (740) 533-4310, open weekdays 8 to 4. Under section 319.202, the buyer files a statement of value, the seller pays the conveyance fee and the auditor endorses the deed.

The state charge in section 319.54(G)(3) is $1 or ten cents per $100, whichever is more, and a county can add a transfer tax capped at thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. Counties choose their own totals, so the quickest check is the Conveyance Fee Calculator in the Tools menu of the auditor's site, which includes the parcel transfer fee. This is the southernmost county in Ohio, part of Appalachian Ohio and the Huntington-Ashland metropolitan area, with part of Wayne National Forest inside its lines. Typical value of an owned home in 2020 to 2024, $144,000. Median gross rent, $848. Median household income, $58,325, with 15.0 percent of residents in poverty. Builders took out 23 permits in 2025.

How did House Bill 186 change second half 2025 bills in Lawrence County?

The auditor's home page says the Inflation Cap Credit appears on second half 2025 real estate bills, which were mailed July 9, 2026. It is based on new revenue each school district gained from the 20 mill floor measured against inflation, and it did not alter any appraised value. A buyer or title agent can view the credit by searching the parcel on the auditor's site.

An owner who paid before the credit was applied needs to do nothing, because any overpayment rolls into the 2026 first half bill. Ask the auditor how a carried credit should show on a closing statement.

Which tools does the Lawrence County auditor offer sellers?

Beyond the calculator, the auditor's Tools menu holds a Tax Estimator, a Sales Report, a Sales List and a Delinquency Report. The sales reports list recent sales in the county, which helps when you set a price. The auditor's site also carries a GIS parcel viewer through its map link, and a search page that shows the appraisal and payment history for any parcel.

The recorder accepts it and adds $20.00. The 3 inch top margin on page one is reserved for the recorder, auditor and engineer. Court papers, plats, DD214s, state or federal documents and older instruments are exempt from the rule.

  • Warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds and limited warranty deeds.
  • Executor's, administrator's, guardian's, trustee's and sheriff's deeds.
  • Certificates of transfer and transfer on death designation affidavits.
  • Mortgages, assignments, modifications, satisfactions and releases of lien.
  • Affidavits on facts relating to title, affidavits of surviving spouse and affidavits of successor trustee.
  • Memoranda of trust, powers of attorney, land contracts and easements.
  • Mechanic's liens, lis pendens notices and Medicaid estate recovery liens and their releases.

Military discharges and veteran grave summaries record without a fee under the same table. Federal tax liens carry their own listed charge of $5.00.

What happens at the Licking County auditor before the recorder?

No deed skips the auditor. Under section 319.202 the grantee, or an agent, declares the value conveyed, and the auditor stamps the deed with the fee. An exempt transfer needs only a stated reason.

Per the auditor's page, since May 1, 2026 a conveyance, exempt transfer, split or merge has to arrive by 4 p.m. to clear that day. That office is at 20 South Second Street, (740) 670-5040.

Sellers pay the state conveyance fee there. A county real property transfer tax would be collected at the same counter only if commissioners had enacted one under section 322.02, at no more than 30 cents per $100. Learn from the auditor whether it exists before choosing a closing date. When it does exist, payment precedes the trip to the recorder.

How can you search and watch Licking County records?

The recorder publishes a PaxWorld public access site at apps.lickingcounty.gov. It asks users to create an account with a username and password. Images that a user buys download to the user's computer, so the site tells visitors to allow downloads in the browser.

The same page promotes an AlertMe service that sends a notification when a document is recorded in your name. Older records can be searched at the recorder's counter, where the index is free.

Title companies, law firms and banks that file often can use eRecording. The county's page names four vendors:

  • CSC eRecording Solutions
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile

The recorder says electronic filing can cut turnaround from three to five working days to minutes or hours, and payment of recording fees is handled electronically.

What does the Census Bureau report about Licking County housing?

The Census Bureau QuickFacts table tallies 73,930 housing units for July 2025 and 68,620 households across the 2020 to 2024 survey years. Owned homes are valued around $275,200, and about three in four are lived in by the owner. Rent averages $1,078, and a homeowner with a loan pays about $1,693 monthly.

Population rose from 178,501 in April 2020 to an estimated 185,564 in July 2025. Newark is the county seat, and Wikipedia lists Heath, Johnstown, New Albany, Pataskala and Reynoldsburg as the other cities.

How does a payoff or an inheritance show up in the Licking County record?

A sale usually produces more than one recorded paper. The buyer's deed goes on record, and the seller's old mortgage is cleared by a satisfaction or release that the lender files. The state sheet lists satisfaction, release, partial release and cancellation as separate document types, and a marginal reference costs $4 when the recorder notes a link to an earlier filing.

Inherited property follows a different path. An executor's or administrator's deed, a certificate of transfer or a transfer on death designation affidavit can move title without a conventional sale, and each one is recorded like any other deed. If the owner received Medicaid benefits, the state table also lists a Medicaid estate recovery lien and its release as recordable instruments. Anyone who spots one of these in the chain should raise it with the title company before closing.

Veterans can record a military discharge with the recorder. The recorder's page names veterans discharges among the documents it accepts, and the state fee table shows no charge for a military discharge. Census data counts 11,370 veterans in Licking County for 2020 to 2024.

What should you know about Licking County's boundaries when searching old deeds?

The legislature carved Licking County out of Fairfield County in 1808, so the earliest history of a parcel may sit under the parent county's name. The recorder's holdings go back to the early 1800s, and the staff will help a searcher read the index. Seven counties touch Licking County, which means a parcel near a county line can carry a description that mentions Knox, Delaware, Franklin or another neighbor.

A rural parcel adds another wrinkle. The county ranks 11th among Ohio's 88 counties for farm products sold, and Wikipedia reports frequent developer offers for farmland near New Albany. A deed search for acreage should cover every transfer and any easements. The state table lists agricultural easements and conservation easements as their own document types.

More questions about Licking County, OH Recorder of Deeds

When is the Licking County recorder open?

Staff are in from 8 AM until 4:30 PM on weekdays, and recording itself happens between 8:30 AM and 4:15 PM. Call (740) 670-5300 before a holiday.

What would a two-page Licking County deed cost to record?

The county sheet lists $39.00 for one to two pages, and its formula is pages times $8 plus $23. A third page brings the printed fee to $47.00.

Is searching Licking County records free?

Searching the index and record books at the recorder's counter is free. The online PaxWorld site requires an account, and purchased images download from the site.

Do I need the auditor before I record a Licking County deed?

Yes, the auditor endorses the deed and collects the conveyance fee first. For same-day processing the deed must reach the auditor by 4 p.m.

Can a title company e-record in Licking County?

Yes, the recorder accepts electronic filings through four listed eRecording vendors. Recorded documents come back electronically.

Logan County by the numbers

Which Bellefontaine office accepts a Logan County deed?

The Logan County recorder sits in the annex at 100 S. Madriver Street, Bellefontaine, OH 43311. The recorder's page gives 937-599-7201 as the phone number and lists the office as open Monday through Friday from 8:00 until 4:30. Wednesday is the day the office issues Veteran ID cards.

The office describes itself as keeper of the land ownership record and of every lien against land. It lists work under more than 1,000 Revised Code sections, stores records in archival form and indexes each filing so a searcher can trace ownership forward in time. Title examiners, attorneys, genealogists and historians all use those files.

The Logan Online portal lists a Recorder's Document Search for looking up filed documents. The recorder also publishes Document Standardization Guidelines, a historical page and a Veteran ID Card Program page.

What does the Logan County recorder charge?

A short schedule appears on the county's recordable documents page. Everything the recorder collects goes into the county general fund.

Logan County document filing fees
ItemFee
First 2 pages$39
Each additional page$8
Non-standardization fee$20
Marginal reference, each$4

Source: Logan County Recordable Documents.

Phone 937-599-7201 for a total on a lengthy document.

What layout rules can trigger the $20 fee in Logan County?

The extra $20 applies to paper that ignores Ohio Revised Code 317.114. Logan County's guidelines page ties the rule to documents prepared after June 30, 2009, and spells out the specifications:

  • Type no smaller than 10 point.
  • Sheets between letter size and legal size, meaning 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Ink in black or blue, with no highlighter marks.
  • One inch of white space along both sides and the foot of each page.
  • Three inches blank at the head of page one, held for stamps from the recorder, auditor and engineer.
  • An inch and a half blank at the head of every later page.

Five categories fall outside the rule: papers from a court or a taxing authority, plats, DD-214 discharge forms, state or federal documents, and anything signed before the law took effect. The page also offers a downloadable template.

What does the Logan County auditor do before the recorder?

A deed visits the county auditor first, and that office shares the 100 S. Madriver Street address. The auditor's forms page names the paperwork that can come into play:

  • Conveyance Form DTE 100 for an ordinary sale, and DTE 100M for a manufactured home.
  • Exempt Conveyance DTE 100EX, or 100MEX for a manufactured home.
  • Agriculture Conveyance DTE 102.
  • Homestead Conveyance DTE 101.
  • Owner Occupied Credit Application DTE 105C and the Homestead Exemption Application DTE 105A.
  • Destroyed Property Application DTE 26 for a building that no longer stands.

Logan County also posts a Survey and Conveyance Standards PDF for legal descriptions and an online Conveyance Fee Calculator. The state conveyance fee falls on the grantor under section 319.202, and a county transfer tax joins it only where commissioners adopted one under Chapter 322. The auditor can say which charges apply to your sale.

How does a Logan County forfeited land sale reach the recorder?

A parcel that went through tax foreclosure and drew no buyer in two offerings is forfeited to the State of Ohio and remanded to the auditor. The auditor's published auction rules describe a sale at the Logan County Courthouse Annex, 100 S. Madriver Street. Properties sell "As-Is" and "Buyer Beware," and the auditor gives no representation about possession, eviction or prior inspection.

The high bidder gets an Auditor's Deed. According to the rules, the auditor files it with the recorder and delivers it to the purchaser, and ownership passes at the moment the deed is delivered to the recorder. That deed extinguishes earlier title except for taxes and assessments not yet due, federal tax liens, easements and covenants running with the land. The rules bar a delinquent taxpayer or a current owner of the parcel from buying.

Bidders pay everything or leave at least $1,000 per parcel on sale day, and the remainder is due within 10 calendar days. The 2021 version of the rules also adds a 50 cent per parcel transfer charge and a 50 cent per parcel charge for envelope and postage, on top of recording.

When do Logan County property taxes come due, and how often is value reset?

The treasurer's site gave July 22, 2026 as the second-half due date and counted 38,426 parcels. The office sits at 100 S. Madriver Street, Suite D, and answers at (937) 599-7223 on weekdays between 8:00 AM and 4:30 PM. A county FAQ also describes an automatic withdrawal option that pulls the bill from a bank account on the last due date.

The auditor's FAQ lays out the cycle: a reappraisal each six years and a possible adjustment in the third calendar year after it. Taxable value is 35 percent of appraised value. The Ohio Department of Taxation's schedule puts Logan County in a 2028 update and a 2031 reappraisal. Formal complaints go to the Board of Revision, which accepts them from January 1 through March 31. Three officeholders sit on the board, the auditor, the treasurer and the president of the commissioners, or their representatives, and an owner can bring appraisals or comparable sales to the hearing.

What do county history and Census data say about Logan County?

Logan County lies in west central Ohio. The recorder's history page says it was cut from northern Champaign County in 1818 and named for Benjamin Logan. Hardin County was carved out of its northern portion in 1820 and began running its own affairs in 1833. Bellefontaine is the seat and only city, and Wikipedia places Campbell Hill, Ohio's highest natural point at 1,549 feet, northeast of the city.

Survey figures for 2020 to 2024 appear in the Census Bureau QuickFacts table:

  • Population reached 46,302 in July 2025, a 0.3 percent change from April 2020.
  • Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $203,200, and 77.6 percent of housing is owner-occupied.
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,326 with a loan, $601 without.
  • Rent at the median: $845 gross.
  • The 19,560 households report a median income of $71,551.
  • 24,071 housing units stood in the county in July 2025, and 120 permits were issued in 2025.

What is the recorder's role in Ohio, and what is Torrens land?

The recorder's history reaches back to the Northwest Territory of 1787, which gave every county such an office. Statehood in 1803 brought a rule that common pleas judges name the recorder. Voters took over the choice in 1829, and a four-year term has applied since 1936.

The recorder's page also covers Torrens registration. Where land is registered under the Torrens Act, its boundaries are certified and a state insurance fund backs the title, and the recorder handles those registered land records. A seller who owns an unusual rural tract should ask the Logan recorder whether any part of it was registered.

The auditor, the treasurer and the recorder all list 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine as their address, so a closing agent can take the transfer, the tax question and the recording to one building.

More questions about Logan County, OH Recorder of Deeds

What is the filing fee for a short Logan County deed?

The posted schedule charges $39 for the opening two pages, then $8 for every page after that. A document that misses the layout standards picks up $20 more.

When can I visit the Logan County recorder?

The office at 100 S. Madriver Street in Bellefontaine opens weekdays at 8:00 and closes at 4:30. Its phone number is 937-599-7201.

Which papers skip the Logan County layout fee?

Court and taxing authority papers, plats, DD-214 discharge forms and state or federal documents are exempt, along with anything executed before the law began.

Does the Logan County recorder help fill out deed forms?

The office keeps and indexes records. Have a title company or attorney draft the deed, and phone 937-599-7201 with filing questions.

When does a forfeited land buyer own the property in Logan County?

Ownership passes when the auditor hands the Auditor's Deed to the recorder, according to the published auction rules. The auditor then sends the recorded deed to the purchaser.

Which Elyria office files a Lorain County deed?

The Lorain County Recorder files it. The office is in Room 102 at 226 Middle Avenue, Elyria, OH 44035, answers 440-329-5148, and posts weekday hours of 8 AM to 4 PM on its website.

The Recorder keeps the land record and nothing else. Its FAQ page says staff do not supply blank forms, fill them in, alter a deed, decide ownership disputes, or search for liens for you. A title company or attorney covers those jobs. The same page says county records go back to 1824, and that you can download a free copy of your own deed from the online property search, with certified copies available at the counter.

What is the Lorain County Recorder's fee for a deed?

Two pages of a deed cost $39.00 on the Recorder's 2026 fee page, and the price climbs by $8.00 with every added page. Each printed side is a page, so a deed printed on both faces of two sheets counts as four.
